americas.title: ROTA NANNY with Special Needs Experience
americas.salary: : $150,000/year Health Stipend: $500/month Benefits: PTO + Performance-Based Annual Bonus; potential retention bonus Travel: Domestic & International Travel Required Start Date: As Soon As Possible Position: Two ROTA Nannies working opposite rotations ABOUT THE ROLE A private family in Miami is seeking two highly experienced Special Needs ROTA Nannies to provide exceptional, full-charge, surrogate caregiving roles care for a happy, playful, 2 year old boy with Williams syndrome. The boy is minimally affected, he is a normal happy little boy who is in need of love and care. This is a significant, long-term position requiring a Nanny who can become a consistent and deeply involved presence in the child's life. The ideal candidate will combine strong special-needs experience with an educational, developmental approach to childcare and have the maturity, confidence, structure, and warmth necessary to support the child's continued growth. The child maintains an active weekly schedule that includes developmental appointments and therapies Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally reserved for enriching activities, museums, parks, playdates, swimming, and opportunities for social development. The family is particularly interested in candidates with a child development, early childhood education, special education, nursing, or comparable professional background. WILLIAMS SYNDROME / SPECIAL NEEDS CARE YOU MUST HAVE AT LEAST 8 YEARS EXPERIENCE WITH SPECIAL NEEDS TODDLERS. The child is minimally affected, he runs around, loves to play and is in desperate need of enrichment and entertainment from a creative caregiver. Williams syndrome experience is highly valued but is not required. Candidates must, however, have substantial professional experience caring for children with special needs, developmental differences, genetic conditions, or comparable care requirements. The selected Nannies will receive detailed training and handoff information regarding this child's specific presentation, routines, care protocols, therapies, nutrition, and developmental needs. The current Nanny and members of the child's professional care team will assist with the transition. The child is independently mobile and currently participates in OT, PT, speech, and other developmental services. Candidates should be comfortable attending appointments and implementing recommendations from specialists into his daily routine. RESPONSIBILITIES Provide full-charge, developmentally appropriate care during ON rotations - your hours of work are the hours that the boy is awake, usually from 7am - 7:30pm or later at times. Maintain a structured, predictable, and nurturing daily routine Attend and coordinate therapy, developmental, and medical appointments Reinforce recommendations from OT, PT, speech, and other specialists Encourage speech, communication, independence, and social development - make friends with other nannies in the areas, set up playdates so he can have friends. He needs that for development and especially because he will be going into preschool soon. Create age-appropriate educational and sensory activities Research and arrange museums, parks, classes, playdates, and enriching outings Encourage opportunities for friendships and peer interaction Prepare and oversee appropriate meals and snacks in accordance with the child's nutritional guidelines Maintain awareness of Williams syndrome-related care considerations and family-established protocols. You will meet with the current nanny and the specialists. He only goes to 2 appointments a year, he is performing at a peak level, he’s a normal little boy who happens to have a diagnosis, but he’s a joy to be around. Support swimming, outdoor play, and physical development Maintain a detailed written daily journal documenting meals, activities, appointments, developmental observations, and the child's overall status Communicate thoroughly with the opposite ROTA Nanny to ensure seamless handoffs Maintain exceptional discretion and confidentiality at all times The family is seeking someone who will be proactive rather than passive. This Nanny should naturally research activities, create opportunities for development and socialization, and take ownership of creating a fulfilling daily life for the child. ROTA & TRAVEL The family is open to either a 7 days on/7 days off or 14 days on/14 days off rotation, depending upon the final ROTA team. The family maintains an international lifestyle, and the Nannies must be genuinely comfortable with extended travel. Travel may include up to 3 months in Canada and shorter trips to Europe for the father’s business, with periods of approximately one month or longer outside Miami. The ROTA Nannies will continue alternating rotations while the family is traveling. Candidates must have the flexibility and personal circumstances necessary to accommodate extended international travel throughout the year. IDEAL CANDIDATE The strongest candidate will be: You are well rounded, kind, patient and loving. Ok with ROTA live-in. The family will provide accommodations when traveling or when you are working. You will have accommodations nearby the house probably if you are expected to stay nearby, otherwise you can fly home. You have a stable home life and are not distracted with any personal matters which allows you to focus truly on the care of the child for a deeply committed, long term career. (If you have children, pets, or family that requires you to be home often, this schedule would likely interfere with your lifestyle and would not be the right fit.) ROTA experience is required. Childhood Education Background, Strongly Preferred. Highly experienced with special-needs children, although this child is minimally affected, he is in dire need of someone who understands what he needs as far as nutrition, affection, stimulation and developmental support as he currently does not have that type of support. He is a happy little boy and easy to care for. Educated in child development, early childhood education, special education, nursing, or a related discipline The household is newly staffed, which means that there is not a whole lot of structure, the family would love for the boy to have that type of structure with a caregiver. Someone who can set great routines as best as possible with the travel schedule. During the school year, once the boy enters pre-school, there will be more structure. You need to be emotionally mature, able to work in environments where the parents are unavailable for consult. You will report to the office manager. You are self managing and stable in personality. If you are reactive, highly emotional or cannot self-regulate, this is not the right job for you. The boy needs someone solid as a rock. He needs someone that he can count on consistently. Experienced in full-charge private childcare; and experience acting as a surrogate caregiver. Confident and capable of making appropriate decisions independently Structured, organized, and consistent Warm, affectionate, and genuinely engaged with children Creative and naturally inclined toward educational play Knowledgeable about child nutrition and healthy development Comfortable collaborating with therapists and medical professionals An excellent communicator and detailed record keeper Mature, emotionally stable, and professional Able to maintain firm but appropriate boundaries and structure Comfortable working autonomously Highly discreet and accustomed to maintaining confidentiality Flexible with international travel Seeking a serious, long-term position HOUSEHOLD The family's primary residence is an approximately 8,000-square-foot home in Pinecrest, Miami. The Nanny will work closely with the family's Office Manager, who assists with household and staff scheduling. Household cleaning and maintenance are handled separately, allowing the Nanny's primary focus to remain on the child. The Nanny and child will generally eat meals together. This position requires someone who is comfortable operating independently within a private household and who does not require extensive day-to-day supervision. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Base Salary: $150,000/year Health Stipend: $500/month Paid Time Off: Provided Bonus: Performance-based annual bonus Retention Bonus: Potentially available Expenses: Family-provided expense card for approved groceries, activities, and child-related expenses Travel Expenses: Family-paid for required work travel REQUIREMENTS Candidates must have substantial professional childcare experience with demonstrated special-needs experience. Candidates should also possess: Excellent professional references CPR/First Aid certification Valid driver's license and clean driving record Valid passport and ability to travel internationally Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong understanding of confidentiality and private-family boundaries Ability to commit to a demanding ROTA lifestyle and extended international travel Direct Williams syndrome experience is welcomed but is not an absolute requirement. The family is prioritizing candidates with exceptional special-needs experience, strong developmental knowledge, maturity, confidence, and the ability to provide consistent, long-term care. Job TypeFull-TimeJob CategoriesGoverness | NannyHousingLive-in or On-siteCompensation$150K-175K DOE

americas.title: Executive Housekeeper / Household Assistant | Private Palm Beach Residence
americas.salary: : $40–$50+/hour DOE + Stipend for the Right Candidate Schedule: Full-time, Year-Round; Monday - Friday 9:00 am - 5:00 pm; with seasonal flexibility required Position Overview A private couple is seeking an experienced, polished and highly dependable Executive Housekeeper / Household Assistant to take ownership of the day-to-day care and smooth operation of their Florida residence. This is a year-round position in a semi-casual home with high expectations for cleanliness, organization, discretion and attention to detail. The ideal candidate understands private service and takes genuine pride in maintaining a beautifully cared-for home. The Principals are typically in-residence November through April. During season, the household is more active, and the successful candidate must have ultimate flexibility with their schedule to accommodate the needs of the family. When the Principals are not in residence, the schedule becomes considerably more predictable and relaxed; however, the same high standard of care and accountability is expected year-round. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking for a long-term position who enjoys becoming an integral and trusted part of a household. Responsibilities The Executive Housekeeper / Household Assistant will take ownership of the overall condition, organization and readiness of the residence, including: Detailed daily and routine housekeeping throughout the home Maintaining bedrooms, bathrooms, kitchen and living areas to a consistently high standard Laundry, linens, wardrobe care and coordination of dry cleaning Maintaining organized closets, cupboards, refrigerators and storage areas Monitoring and replenishing household, kitchen and personal-care supplies Grocery shopping, household shopping and local errands Maintaining household inventories and anticipating needs before supplies run low Receiving deliveries and ensuring items are properly unpacked and stored Coordinating access for approved vendors, trades and service providers Identifying maintenance or household issues and communicating them promptly Completing seasonal deep-cleaning, organization and household projects Preparing the residence for the Principals' arrival and ensuring it remains guest-ready Assisting with additional household needs as they arise Cooking & Meal Preparation: Someone who genuinely enjoys cooking or meal preparation would be especially well suited for this household. This is not a private chef position; however, the ability and willingness to assist with simple, fresh meals and food preparation is an important part of the role. Responsibilities may include: Grocery shopping and maintaining a well-stocked kitchen Preparing simple meals, proteins, vegetables, sides and snacks Batch cooking and meal preparation Portioning and properly storing prepared foods Keeping the refrigerator organized and monitoring freshness Preparing or assembling meals that can easily be reheated later Maintaining an ongoing grocery and food-preparation plan Seasonal Schedule & Flexibility November–April | Principals in Residence This is the household's active season. The successful candidate must have significant schedule flexibility and understand that the family's needs will dictate the flow of the workweek. While there will be a general schedule, this is not a position for someone who requires rigid start and end times. Some days may require earlier starts, later evenings, schedule adjustments, additional errands, vendor appointments or increased household support. May–October | Principals Away / Reduced Residence The schedule is more relaxed and predictable during the off-season, providing an opportunity to focus on projects that can be difficult to accomplish while the household is fully occupied. This may include deep cleaning, detailed organization, inventory, closets and storage, household projects, maintenance coordination and preparing the residence for the upcoming season. The off-season is also the preferred time for PTO, personal appointments and planned time away whenever possible, allowing greater availability to the family during their months in residence. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is: Experienced working in a high-end private residence Mature, professional, discreet and trustworthy Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail Proactive and naturally anticipates household needs Comfortable working independently without a daily task list Flexible and understands the changing demands of a seasonal residence An excellent communicator Resourceful and willing to pitch in wherever needed Comfortable with grocery shopping, errands and household organization Someone who enjoys cooking and meal preparation Looking for a stable, long-term position and household to call home professionally Above all, the family is seeking someone who takes true ownership of the residence and is looking for a long-term fit. The right person notices what needs attention, anticipates needs, creates a plan and follows through without waiting to be asked—taking the same pride in the care, organization and details of the home whether the Principals are in residence or away. This is an excellent opportunity for a seasoned private service professional who enjoys leading by example, maintaining impeccable standards, and working collaboratively within a household team. The ideal candidate is an exceptional housekeeper with strong wardrobe management and organizational skills who takes pride in creating beautifully maintained, highly organized spaces. This individual will serve as the lead housekeeper, helping establish consistency, improve communication, and provide day-to-day guidance to the housekeeping team while fostering a collaborative and supportive work environment. The family is looking for someone who can bring stability, professionalism, and positive leadership to the team. Excellent English communication skills, discretion, and respect for privacy are essential. The family is hoping to have someone in place before the start of the school year and is open to beginning with a paid trial. Key Responsibilities Executive Housekeeping Maintain assigned areas of the residence to impeccable standards of cleanliness and presentation. Perform detailed housekeeping, including dusting, vacuuming, mopping, polishing, sanitizing, and general upkeep. Launder, iron, steam, fold, and properly care for clothing, linens, and delicate fabrics. Maintain organized closets, wardrobes, and storage areas, ensuring belongings are consistently returned to their proper place. Clean and organize kitchen spaces, assist with kitchen prep, and maintain an orderly environment throughout the day. Monitor household supplies and communicate inventory needs. Wardrobe & Laundry Management Manage the principals' personal laundry with exceptional attention to detail. Properly organize and return clothing to designated locations within the principals' wardrobes. Exercise discretion and respect for privacy while working with personal belongings. Partner with the House Manager on wardrobe and closet organization projects as needed. Manage all dry cleaning, including drop-off, pick-up, and quality control. Team Collaboration & Leadership Work alongside two additional housekeepers and a houseman within a collaborative household team. Help coordinate responsibilities across designated housekeeping zones to ensure seamless daily coverage. Lead by example while helping establish clear communication, accountability, and consistency among the housekeeping staff. Encourage open communication and help create an environment where team members feel comfortable asking questions and providing feedback. Collaborate closely with the House Manager to maintain efficient household operations. Household Support Assist with preparing the home for guests, family gatherings, and special occasions. Support additional household projects and responsibilities as needed. Occasional light meal preparation is a plus but not required. Childcare experience is welcomed but not required. A valid driver's license with a clean driving record is strongly preferred. Qualifications Previous experience as an Executive Housekeeper or Lead Housekeeper in a private residence required. Experience working in a fully staffed household strongly preferred. Exceptional wardrobe management, closet organization, laundry, ironing, and luxury garment care experience. Strong organizational skills with meticulous attention to detail. Excellent English communication skills. Professional, discreet, and respectful of personal space and confidentiality. Positive, collaborative leadership style with the ability to work well within a team. Comfortable receiving and providing constructive feedback. Valid driver's license and clean driving record preferred. Schedule Monday – Friday Approximately - 7:00 AM – 3:00 PM No weekends The housekeeping team generally works the same daytime schedule to ensure collaboration and consistent coverage throughout the home. The children attend school during the day, making this an excellent opportunity for an experienced professional who genuinely enjoys working with young children while also thriving in the organization, care, and daily operation of a sophisticated private residence. The family is seeking someone who is energetic, hardworking, proactive, detail-oriented, dependable, and highly organized. The ideal candidate understands the standards and expectations of an ultra-high-net-worth household and is comfortable caring for a home containing fine furnishings, specialty materials, and high-end finishes that require specific care. Kitchen & Daily Household Organization Responsibilities include loading and unloading dishwashers; putting away clean dishes; handwashing appropriate cookware, knives, pots, and pans; wiping and maintaining kitchen surfaces; taking out trash and recycling; and keeping the kitchen organized and properly stocked. Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, and more. Typical schedule: This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week role. Academic instruction typically takes place Monday through Thursday from approximately 9:00 a.m.– 3:00 p.m., with remaining hours dedicated to lesson preparation and engaging the children in activities after academic work is complete. Fridays are generally focused on enrichment activities and outings. Flexibility is an important part of the role, and the educator must be comfortable adjusting their schedule as family needs, travel, special events, or learning opportunities arise, including occasional evenings, weekends, and overnights. Time off: Intensive periods are balanced with generous breaks, including summer, holidays, and extended leave. Perks: Family travel opportunities, special events, and theme park access, including Disney and Universal. Flexibility: The schedule adjusts around family travel and lifestyle needs, including agreed-upon nights, weekends, overnights, and occasional short-notice travel. What You’ll Do Provide daily, in-home instruction and mentorship for two elementary-aged children using the family’s established homeschool program, while adapting lessons to each child’s learning style and needs. Collaborate closely with parents on academic goals, behavioral expectations, routines, travel schedules, and family priorities; communicate proactively about progress, challenges, and upcoming plans. Build on the core curriculum with hands-on projects, reading, arts, nature, physical activity, community outings, and other experiential learning opportunities. Familiarity with the Abeka curriculum is a plus, but not required. Support neurodiverse children using calm, consistent, developmentally appropriate strategies. Set clear expectations and healthy boundaries while remaining patient, warm, composed, and dependable—even during emotionally heightened moments or transitions. Remain actively engaged after formal schoolwork is complete by initiating play, creative activities, conversation, outdoor time, life-skills practice, and other meaningful connection—not simply concluding the day when lessons end. Plan weekly enrichment experiences and field trips, including a regular Friday outing, and prepare purposeful, age-appropriate, enjoyable activities. When traveling, research the destination in advance and create relevant educational and recreational experiences that connect learning to the family’s surroundings. Manage homeschool logistics, including lesson preparation, materials, organized learning spaces, progress tracking, scheduling, and safe transportation as needed. Maintain structure, composure, and consistency during travel, routine changes, and occasional parental absences, helping the children feel secure and supported. What We’re Looking For Availability: Available to start by the end of September 2026. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Special Education, Child Development, or a closely related field. A master’s degree is preferred. Experience: At least two years of relevant experience teaching, mentoring, or caring for elementary-aged children; private education, governess, special education, behavioral-support, or family-based experience is strongly preferred. Behavioral expertise: Demonstrated experience supporting neurodiverse children, including children with ADHD, attention-related needs, emotional-regulation challenges, or impulse-control needs, is required. Presence: Calm, confident, firm, patient, warm, and supportive, with the ability to remain composed and consistent during challenging situations. You can establish authority without harshness and offer warmth without sacrificing consistency. Engagement: Genuinely enjoys spending time with children and naturally initiates play, activities, exploration, and connection beyond formal instruction. Planning: Proactive, organized, and able to anticipate needs, prepare ahead, and independently create thoughtful learning and enrichment plans. Communication: Strong judgment and interpersonal skills, with the maturity to build trust, receive feedback, communicate candidly, and work in close partnership with parents. Adaptability: Comfortable moving between teacher, mentor, activity planner, travel companion, and steady adult presence as the day requires. Location: Resides in or near Windermere, Florida, or is willing to relocate or commute. Relocation may be considered for an exceptional fit. Travel: Able to fulfill the role’s essential domestic travel requirements, including occasional weekends, overnights, extended trips, and short-notice travel, with reasonable accommodation where applicable. Professionalism: Highly reliable, discreet, safety-minded, and committed to providing continuity for the children and family. Next Steps and Application Instructions Please submit your resume, a cover letter explaining why this unique blend of private education, behavioral support, family partnership, enrichment, and travel appeals to you, and three professional references. If possible, include at least one reference from a family, private-educator placement, school leader, or supervisor who has observed your work directly with children. In your letter, please share specific professional examples of your experience supporting children with ADHD, attention or impulse-control needs, or emotional-regulation challenges; establishing kind but firm boundaries; and creating engaging experiences that supported both academic and social-emotional growth.
